newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Laporte restructure on target.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Laporte restructure on target.

text.p: Specialty chemicals group Laporte Plc said on Monday its restructuring program is on target to deliver cost savings of 10 million stg a year in 1997.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, chief executive Jim Leng also said he expects progress on further disposals on non-core businesses to be announced "before long" and set out tough targets for return on capital employed, working capital and profit margins.
Laporte said interim pretax profit slumped to 36.4 million pounds from 67.0 million a year before, mainly due to 23.9 million pounds of exceptional charges related to disposals.

Leng said the restructuring announced six months ago "is going according to plan. We are on budget, on time and delivering the benefits we said." Around two-thirds of the 10 million stg cost saving goal will be achieved in 1996, he said.

Raw material costs, which were key to a disappointing performance in the second half of 1995, have stabilised at lower levels, Leng said, adding: "I think it will trend along those lines" for the rest of the year.
But he declined to go beyond Laporte's formula of forecasting "solid progress" for 1996 as a whole, with "current markets remaining competitive and some markets subdued."

"We are heading in the right direction," Leng said. "We fired on three and a half cylinders out of five in the first half." Laporte, which left its interim payout to shareholders unchanged at 8.5 pence, said the full-year dividend will be based on general progress, a stance Leng said is "realistic."

The restructuring led to a 31 million stg charge against 1995 results. Sales of peripheral businesses were a key element of the moves, and Laporte has announced around 49 million stg of sales so far this year. Leng estimated that 20 to 30 million stg of businesses remain to be sold, and the group is now in a position to think about fresh acquisitions.
"We are thinking about other moves now," Leng said. "We are looking for market leadership and focus on growth sectors."
He said Laporte is "light in the Far East, but equally I could see us wanting businesses in Europe and North America."

Profit margins at Laporte's core divisions were 11.9 percent in the first half, still trailing Laporte's mid-term objective of being "well into the teens." Leng said it is also aiming to achieve return on capital employed "in the mid 20s," compared to below 20 percent last year, and to cut working capital as a percentage of sales by 3 percentage points, making it one of the best in the sector and freeing 30 to 40 million pounds of cash.

Laporte saw a 37 percent fall in operating profit at its specialty organics division, which accounts for nearly 20 percent of sales, as it continued to be hit by problems in the bulk polymer industry. Adhesivies, sealants and coatings and the hygiene and process division also saw falls in profits.

Profits at absorbents and pigments rose 12 percent to 17.2 million stg, despite a decline in profit margins, while in compounds and electronics, profits jumped 45 percent to 20.2 million stg, a performance Leng desribed as "excellent." -- Jonathan Birt, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
